cards.a: Missing VLANs, wrong port assignment, trunk filtering, and native VLAN mismatch. Symptoms are no reachability within a subnet or traffic crossing the wrong VLANs.

cards.q: What is the VLAN verification chain?
cards.a: show vlan, show interfaces status, show interfaces trunk, then show mac address-table. The VLAN must exist and carry the port.

cards.q: What are the usual suspects for VLAN failures?
cards.a: The trunk allowed VLAN list and native VLAN mismatch.

cards.q: What must be true before a port assignment takes effect?
cards.a: The VLAN must exist. A VLAN must be created before switchport access vlan works.

cards.q: How do you force an access port to a VLAN?
cards.a: Use switchport mode access and switchport access vlan 10.

cards.q: What does a trunk carry across the link?
cards.a: Only the allowed VLANs listed in the trunk configuration (switchport trunk allowed vlan).

cards.q: What is the impact of a native VLAN mismatch between trunk ends?
cards.a: It causes silent breakage, including control-plane and cross-VLAN traffic issues because the untagged native VLAN must match on both ends.

cards.q: What is the default native VLAN on a trunk?
What proves which VLAN a host lives in?
cards.a: The MAC address table (show mac address-table vlan 10), which is ground truth of VLAN membership.

cards.q: Why is show vlan not the same as what a trunk passes?
cards.a: show vlan lists VLANs on the switch, while the trunk allowed list gates which VLANs actually cross the trunk link.

cards.q: What command shows detailed port-to-VLAN assignment?
cards.a: show interfaces <if> switchport. The no switchport command turns a port into a Layer 3 (routed) port.

cards.q: No DHCP across VLANs is most likely caused by what?
cards.a: A missing IP helper (ip helper-address) on the interface
